newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S., China set textile talks in Beijing next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China set textile talks in Beijing next week.

text.p: The United States and China will hold talks in Beijing next week to try to solve a dispute over American penalties on imports of Chinese textiles, a U.S. embassy official said on Friday.
Rita Hayes, the chief textile negotiator of the U.S. Trade Representative Office, will be in Beijing on Monday for the talks, the official said.
China has threatened to temporarily ban imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks in retaliation for U.S. curbs on its textile products.
In September, the United States set penalties of $19 million on Chinese imports, saying Beijing was shipping textiles through third countries to avoid quota restrictions.
China has said the penalties were imposed without sufficient evidence and without full consultation.
It has said its own import ban would go into effect on December 10 if there was no resolution of the dispute.
The two sides also must agree to extend a bilateral textile agreement which expires at the end of this year. The U.S. penalties were imposed under the textile accord.
